title: Good ideas die when they get a “rationalist” skin
summary:
DefenderOfBasic basically dropped the hottest PR advice in a meme: smart nerds discover something legit (their example: prediction markets), then accidentally *poison it with their vibe*, so everyone else rejects it on pure “I hate these people” instincts. Their line that stuck was that you then have to do “extra work to undo the aesthetic damage because people are allergic to the good idea” — and they go further: “normies are very open to good ideas,” they’re just (rightfully) reacting to ugly subcultures and weird messengers.

The replies turn into a tug-of-war over whether this is real or just cope. archived_videos pushes back that ideas mostly just fail to distribute by default, so there’s no need for a nerd-scaring-normies theory; DefenderOfBasic counters with “you can expose people to literally the same idea, dressed differently, and their reaction… is going to be 180,” and suggests basically A/B testing it across different social networks. Oszillate calls the whole thing a scapegoat (“pretend they are persecuted-by-nerds”), while BoilingPb points out prediction markets also get kneecapped top‑down (CIA/internal markets, Polymarket legality), and DefenderOfBasic concedes it’s “pressures from both sides.” Jotto999 adds the snarky technical nitpick: r/agedlikemilk isn’t “prediction markets,” because it lacks the actual machinery (criteria, aggregation, profit/loss).

Then it gets a clean real-world “see, this is the phenomenon” cameo: Loomopolis quotes DefenderOfBasic under a RealDoctorMike post about RFK Jr getting praised for saying the same basic nutrition/exercise stuff doctors said for years — identical idea, different messenger, wildly different reception. You care because if you’re trying to spread anything useful (health advice, new institutions, policy tools), the thread’s point is brutal but practical: content matters less than who it’s wearing, and the first group to brand an idea can accidentally make it radioactive for everyone else.
